items.title: Falling Behind Drives Unsafe Development in an Idealised AI Race Experiment
items.desc: A framed behavioural experiment models an AI development race, showing that participants who fall behind competitors become markedly more willing to choose risky, less safety-conscious 'unsafe' development — evidence that competitive pressure itself drives unsafe AI. [arXiv econ.GN, posted 2026-07-28]

items.title: RIDGE: An Autonomous Framework for Validation and Method Discovery in LLM-Generated Option Pricing
items.desc: Introduces an autonomous (agentic) framework that validates option-pricing code generated by large language models, checking that the numerical methods stay mathematically consistent and stable across model parameters — addressing reliability gaps in LLM-written quant finance code. [arXiv q-fin.CP, posted 2026-07-28]

items.title: Robust Hedging Valuation Adjustment for Deep Hedging Policies under Market Frictions
items.desc: Applies a robust hedging valuation adjustment as a post-training step for neural 'deep hedging' policies, quantifying whether a trading desk can actually afford to run a learned hedging strategy under transaction costs and market frictions. [arXiv q-fin.RM, posted 2026-07-28]

items.title: Emergent Latent-State Computation under Stochastic Volatility
items.desc: Uses mechanistic interpretability to study how sequence (deep learning) models internally represent hidden stochastic-volatility states when they observe only returns, offering a controlled financial benchmark for understanding what ML models learn about latent market dynamics. [arXiv q-fin.ST / cs.LG, posted 2026-07-28]

sections.name: 📦 Operations & Supply Chain (INFORMS: Management Science, M&SOM, Operations Research)

items.title: A.I. Companies Are Recruiting Electricians and Carpenters by the Thousands
items.desc: The AI data-center buildout is creating intense demand for skilled trades — electricians, carpenters and other physical labor — making the availability of trained workers a real constraint on AI expansion. [NYT, posted 2026-07-29]

items.title: South Korea's Memory Chip Giant Defies A.I. Market Jitters
items.desc: SK Hynix reported record sales and profits driven by AI memory demand, yet the strong results failed to reassure investors amid a broader selloff in AI-linked chip stocks. [NYT, posted 2026-07-29]

items.title: The Hidden Cost of China's Free A.I.
items.desc: An opinion piece arguing that whichever country supplies the world's cheap or free AI models gains economic and ideological influence, framing China's low-cost model strategy as a competitive and geopolitical challenge for the U.S. [NYT Opinion, posted 2026-07-29]

items.title: A Deluge of A.I. Computing Power Is About to Come Online
items.desc: An interactive analysis showing the installed base of AI chips is roughly doubling every nine months, mapping the scale of the data-center and compute investment boom powering the AI economy. [NYT, posted 2026-07-29]
